title: bus_client dials the loopback port where Python has no AF_UNIX
intention: remote._dial reads bus.port and dials the loopback listener it names where the interpreter has no socket.AF_UNIX, instead of raising UnboundLocalError on rec.
why: Measured 2026-11-20 on akiendell (Windows): every bus call died with 'UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'rec' where it is not associated with a value' at remote.py line 250. Commit f36fa3fae (ticket f62f6b50b047) indented the no-AF_UNIX block under 'if hasattr(socket, "AF_UNIX"):' after that branch's 'return conn, None', so it is dead and rec is never bound. sail chart/cross, outlinecheck and hollow stop on that host.
traces_to: Law 9 (red is the default) and Law 3 (measured); outline 5.4.3: the bus is the only device-to-device path.
how: Dedent lines 245-250 of remote.py out of the AF_UNIX if so they run after 'return conn, None'. Red-first proof deletes socket.AF_UNIX in-process, writes a scratch bus.port naming a stub 127.0.0.1 listener, and asserts _dial returns that connection and the record's key.

clauses.claim: with socket.AF_UNIX deleted and a bus.port record naming a live loopback listener, _dial returns a connection to that listener and the record's key
with socket.AF_UNIX deleted and no bus.port record, _dial raises FileNotFoundError naming bus.port, never UnboundLocalError
with socket.AF_UNIX deleted and a bus.port record naming no port, _dial raises FileNotFoundError saying it names no loopback port

decisions.text: D1: the no-AF_UNIX block in _dial runs after the AF_UNIX branch returns (a dedent).
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, runnable on any host.

measured.saw: sail.py chart 64ae0df3f1f3 raised UnboundLocalError at remote.py:250; the AF_UNIX-less path is dead code after 'return conn, None' (remote.py:245-249); the orchestrator confirmed the same on origin/main
measured.how: traceback of sail chart on akiendell; sed -n 225,250p cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py; git diff 1e958634f HEAD -- remote.py
